text:
alex: Quick bug report from the onboarding sample: intermittent IOException (connection reset) when doing two simultaneous streaming calls from the same OkHttp client on Android emulator. Happens mostly on API 30-31.

maria: Which OkHttp version and are you reusing the same OkHttpClient instance?

alex: OkHttp 4.11.0, yes single client in the sample. Repro steps: open chat list, tap two chats quickly so both start long-polling / streaming. After ~3-6s one stream dies with `java.io.IOException: unexpected end of stream` and the other continues.

lee: Sounds like connection sharing + per-route concurrent streams exhausting the HTTP/1 connection limits. Are you using HTTP/1.1?

alex: Server supports HTTP/2 but on emulator we fall back to HTTP/1. I tested increasing connectionPool size and it reduced frequency. Sample currently uses ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES).

maria: Two small actionable items: 1) Add a short note in the SDK quickstart to reuse a single OkHttpClient and tune ConnectionPool for multi-stream workloads. 2) For streaming use cases prefer HTTP/2 or explicit pooling + keepalive tweaks.

alex: Minimal snippet we landed in the sample:
```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(10, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // zero for long streams
  .build()
```

lee: Also make sure retryOnConnectionFailure(false) if your streams are not idempotent; automatic retry can interleave and cause duplicate partial responses.

alex: Good call. I added that and a short troubleshooting blurb in the sample README. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/140 (draft).

devex-bot: samples/ci: flaky-emulator detected on matrix, please sanity-check emulator network settings.

maria: I'll add two unit/integration tests: concurrent stream smoke on emulator API 31 and a headless HTTP/2 env test. Also adding a one-liner to onboarding: "If streams drop: prefer HTTP/2, tune ConnectionPool, set readTimeout(0), and disable automatic connection retries for non-idempotent streams."

alex: Thanks all 44d. Leaving PR as draft until CI passes.
